cards.front: Untreated severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia can deposit in the brain and cause [___].
cards.context: The feared complication that drives aggressive treatment: very high unconjugated bilirubin crosses the immature blood–brain barrier and deposits in the basal ganglia, causing permanent neurological injury.

cards.front: Infants with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) risk factors get hip ultrasound at 6 weeks; treatment with [___] harness within first weeks of diagnosis is highly effective.
cards.context:
Hip USS is the imaging modality of choice in the first 6 months — femoral head is cartilaginous and not yet ossified (invisible on plain X-ray). After 6 months, X-ray (AP pelvis) becomes useful as the head ossifies.

6-week timing chosen because earlier ligamentous laxity (maternal hormones) creates false positives.

Indications for hip USS at 6 weeks: breech (any time ≥36 weeks), family history, abnormal clinical exam at birth or postnatal check, oligohydramnios, talipes.

cards.front: Newborn metabolic screening includes PKU (preventable intellectual disability with diet) and [___] (hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, prevent fasting).
cards.context:
Two metabolic conditions on the Guthrie panel: phenylketonuria (PKU), where diet prevents phenylalanine neurotoxicity, and MCAD deficiency, where avoiding fasting prevents hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

MCAD (~1:15,000) impairs fatty acid oxidation, so patients can't generate ketones during fasting/illness — presents with hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.

cards.front: Hypertension in pregnancy is SBP ≥[___] and/or DBP ≥90 mmHg on 2 occasions ≥4 h apart (or a single reading ≥160/110).
cards.context:
The pregnancy threshold (140/90) sits below the general adult treatment threshold because mild hypertension matters more here.

Placental perfusion is pressure-dependent, and untreated HTN drives pre-eclampsia, abruption, and IUGR.

Timing reframes the same number. Before 20 weeks, 140/90 is chronic HTN (secondary-cause workup); after 20 weeks it is gestational HTN or pre-eclampsia, triggering an end-organ screen (urinalysis, LFTs, FBC, creatinine).

cards.front: A complete hydatidiform mole is most often karyotype [___] with entirely paternal genetic origin. No fetal tissue is present; malignant risk is 15–20%.
cards.context:
Complete mole: empty ovum fertilised by sperm that duplicates its DNA; most are 46,XX and entirely paternal, with no fetal tissue.

Compared with partial mole, complete mole has higher βhCG and malignant risk. Manage with suction curette, then βhCG surveillance; plateau or rise means persistent GTN.

cards.front: Low-dose [___] started in early pregnancy reduces pre-eclampsia in high-risk women.
cards.context:
The one proven preventive drug: low-dose aspirin started before 16 weeks in high-risk women (previous pre-eclampsia, chronic hypertension, diabetes, etc.) meaningfully reduces pre-eclampsia.

Calcium helps where dietary intake is low.

cards.front: An upper brachial plexus (C5–C6) birth injury causing the 'waiter's tip' posture is [___].
cards.context: The upper trunk (C5–C6) injury from lateral neck traction (often shoulder dystocia) gives the 'waiter's tip' posture — arm adducted, internally rotated, forearm pronated. Most recover with physiotherapy.

cards.front: Prior spontaneous preterm birth <34 weeks PLUS current cervical length ≤25 mm: offer vaginal progesterone and/or cervical [___].
cards.context:
Prior spontaneous preterm birth + current short cervix is the highest-risk group; both interventions can be offered. Vaginal progesterone (200 mg pessary nightly, 16-24 wk until 34-36 wk) cuts preterm birth ~40%.

Cervical cerclage (McDonald suture at 12-14 weeks) is offered for history-indicated (≥3 prior preterm births/losses) or USS-indicated (CL <25 mm with prior preterm birth) cases.

The Arabin pessary is a non-surgical alternative — evidence mixed.

cards.front: Under the 2025 ADIPS criteria, gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic thresholds on 75g OGTT are: fasting ≥5.3, 1-hour ≥[___], or 2-hour ≥9.0 mmol/L.
cards.context:
Even modest maternal hyperglycaemia raises fetal hyperinsulinaemia, macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycaemia, and shoulder dystocia risk.

ADIPS 2025 replaced the 2014 values (5.1 / 10.0 / 8.5); NSW Health notified services in August 2025, so older questions may differ.

cards.front: Oestrogen-containing contraception (COCP, patch, ring) is delayed until [___] weeks postpartum in breastfeeding women; the older concern that it suppresses prolactin and milk supply is not well supported.
cards.context:
RANZCOG no longer supports blanket avoidance during breastfeeding — better-quality studies found no adverse effect on breastfeeding performance or infant outcomes.

Timing is driven by thrombosis, not milk. The puerperium is hypercoagulable and VTE risk peaks in weeks 1-2, so oestrogen waits until that risk has fallen.

cards.front: Preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) occurs between [___]+0 and 36+6 weeks; diagnose with history plus sterile speculum examination, avoiding digital examination unless active labour or birth is imminent.
cards.context:
PPROM means membrane rupture before labour and before 37 weeks; PROM is prelabour rupture at term, while SROM occurs after labour starts.

Diagnose from a history of a gush or persistent leaking, confirmed by sterile speculum examination.

Avoid digital examination unless active labour is established or birth is imminent, because it can introduce vaginal flora and shorten latency.

cards.front: Barlow manoeuvre dislocates a located hip (push posteriorly); [___] manoeuvre reduces a dislocated hip (lift anteriorly). Both lose reliability after 3 months.
cards.context:
The two manoeuvres test opposites. Barlow (push posteriorly) tests if a LOCATED hip can be dislocated — flex, adduct, push posteriorly; positive if 'clunk' as head dislocates.

Ortolani (pull anteriorly) tests if a DISLOCATED hip can be reduced — flex, abduct, lift greater trochanter forward; positive if clunk indicates reduction.

Mnemonic: Barlow Backward, Ortolani Out. Both become unreliable after 3 months as the hip stabilises in dislocation — replaced by Galeazzi sign, limited abduction, asymmetric thigh creases.

cards.front: Preterm birth is birth between 20+0 and 36+6 weeks; affects ~[___]% of Australian pregnancies and is the leading cause of mortality in children <5.
cards.context:
Gestation is written weeks+days, so 20+0 = 20 weeks 0 days and 36+6 = the last day before 37 weeks (term); the 20-week floor is the same threshold that separates preterm birth from miscarriage.

Sub-categorised by severity: late preterm (34-36+6, ~70% of cases, generally good outcomes), moderate (32-33+6), very preterm (28-31+6, significant NICU need), and extremely preterm (<28 weeks).

Even late preterm infants have higher rates of learning difficulties, ADHD, and reduced educational attainment than term peers — which is why prevention matters even near term.

cards.front: The model of antenatal care is determined by risk assessment at the booking visit; high-risk women need [___]-led care.
cards.context:
Risk assessment at booking sorts women into pathways: low-risk women choose between shared care (GP + obstetrician), midwifery group practice (continuity-of-carer with documented reductions in interventions).

Triggers for high-risk pathway: pre-existing HTN, diabetes, autoimmune disease, cardiac disease, BMI >40, prior HDP/stillbirth/preterm birth, multiple pregnancy, significant mental health conditions.

cards.front: Signs of neonatal respiratory distress: tachypnoea >60/min, [___], nasal flaring, recession, cyanosis. Any neonate with these signs needs urgent assessment.
cards.context:
Five classic signs of neonatal respiratory distress: tachypnoea (>60/min), grunting (partial glottis closure for auto-PEEP), nasal flaring, intercostal/subcostal recession, cyanosis.

Combinations escalate urgency (Silverman-Andersen score quantifies).

Differential by gestation + context: TTN (term/near-term post-CS, self-limiting), RDS (preterm, ground-glass CXR), pneumothorax (often after MAS/PPV), MAS (post-term, meconium-stained liquor, patchy infiltrates).

cards.front: Earliest sign of magnesium toxicity is loss of patellar reflexes (~5 mmol/L); antidote is IV [___].
cards.context:
Magnesium toxicity follows a dose-response cascade you can monitor at the bedside without lab access. Therapeutic level is 2-4 mmol/L (anticonvulsant action).

Loss of patellar reflexes appears at ~5 mmol/L — the earliest reliable warning. Respiratory depression follows at ~6-7 mmol/L.

Cardiac conduction abnormalities and arrest at ~12 mmol/L.

cards.front: Universal (rather than ethnicity-based) core reproductive carrier screening covers cystic fibrosis, SMA, and [___].
cards.context:
Most affected children are born to couples without a family history, and self-reported ethnicity poorly predicts carrier status. RANZCOG therefore recommends offering screening regardless of background.

The core panel covers three conditions; expanded screens cover many more. If both partners are carriers, options can include PGT-M with IVF, donor gametes or prenatal diagnosis.

cards.front: First-line manoeuvre for shoulder dystocia is [___] position with suprapubic pressure (NOT fundal); resolves majority of cases.
cards.context:
The mechanism: hyperflexing the maternal hips onto the abdomen rotates the symphysis pubis cephalad and flattens the sacral promontory, straightening the pelvic axis and increasing the AP diameter by 1-2 cm.

Suprapubic (NOT fundal) pressure adds adduction of the anterior shoulder into the oblique diameter.

McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure resolves around 60-90% of shoulder dystocia cases — making it the highest-yield first-line manoeuvre.

cards.front: A complete hydatidiform mole is most often karyotype 46,XX with entirely [___] genetic origin. No fetal tissue is present; malignant risk is 15–20%.
cards.context:
Complete mole: empty ovum fertilised by sperm that duplicates its DNA; most are 46,XX and entirely paternal, with no fetal tissue.

Compared with partial mole, complete mole has higher βhCG and malignant risk. Manage with suction curette, then βhCG surveillance; plateau or rise means persistent GTN.

cards.front: The dating scan is performed at 11-14 weeks; it confirms [___], dates the pregnancy, and detects multiple gestation.
cards.context:
The 11-14 week scan confirms viability, dates pregnancy by CRL, and identifies multiple pregnancy/chorionicity.

Book it in this narrow window because CRL dating is more accurate than later biparietal diameter/head circumference estimates, and chorionicity is easiest to assess while membranes are clearly visible.
